info.name: CanBankX API
info.description:
All business requests route through **KrakenD API Gateway (port 8080)**.
Direct service ports are only used for health checks and internal endpoints not exposed by the gateway.

| Layer | URL |
|---|---|
| KrakenD Gateway | http://localhost:8080 |
| Identity (internal) | http://localhost:8081 |
| Account (internal)  | http://localhost:8082 |
| Payment (internal)  | http://localhost:8083 |
| MailHog (email UI)  | http://localhost:8025 |

**Happy-path flow (with email OTP):**
1. Register Client  → POST /api/clients  *(OTP sent to email)*
2. Verify OTP       → POST /api/clients/{id}/verify  *(otpCode from MailHog inbox)*
3. Login            → POST /api/auth/login  *(real 6-digit OTP sent to email, saves challengeToken)*
4. Verify MFA       → POST /api/auth/mfa  *(otpCode auto-fetched from MailHog via pre-request script)*
5. Create Account   → POST /api/accounts
6. Submit Payment   → POST /api/transactions
7. View Summary     → GET  /api/accounts/{number}/summary

**Happy-path flow (admin bypass):**
1. Register Client  → POST /api/clients
2. Activate Client  → POST /api/clients/{id}/activate
3. (continue from step 3 above)

**MFA flow detail:**
The Login endpoint now generates a real 6-digit OTP and emails it to the client.
The 'Verify MFA' request uses a pre-request script to automatically fetch the OTP
from MailHog (http://localhost:8025) — no manual copy-paste required.
You can also open the MailHog UI in a browser to read the email manually.

KrakenD → POST /identityservice/auth/login
Validates credentials, generates a real 6-digit OTP, and emails it to the client.
Returns a `challengeToken` to include in the MFA step.
Open MailHog (http://localhost:8025) to read the code, or let the 'Verify MFA' pre-request script fetch it automatically.

request.description:
KrakenD → POST /identityservice/auth/mfa
The pre-request script automatically fetches the real 6-digit OTP from MailHog
(http://localhost:8025) by matching the `challengeToken` embedded in the login email.
No manual copy-paste required — just send this request after UC-02 Login.

**If MailHog shows no email:** the OTP is always logged to the identity-service container.
Run:  docker compose logs identity-service | grep MFA-OTP
Then paste the 6-digit code into the `mfa_otp` collection variable manually.

The token is single-use: if the wrong OTP is submitted you must re-run Login to get a new one.

- payment-service  → last 10 transactions    (group: 'recentTransactions')

item.description: Endpoints not exposed by KrakenD. Hit the services directly for debugging or admin use.

request.description: Direct → GET /identityservice/clients
DELETE /identityservice/clients/{id} — marks the client as deactivated (204 No Content).

Direct → POST /identityservice/auth/login
Sends a real 6-digit OTP to the client's email and returns a challengeToken.
Open MailHog (http://localhost:8025) to read the code.

console.warn('No emails found in MailHog inbox.'); return;
console.warn('No MFA email found for challengeToken:', challengeToken); return;
const otpMatch = body.match(/Your login code is:\s*(\d{6})/);
console.log('MFA OTP auto-fetched from MailHog:', otpMatch[1]);
console.warn('Could not extract OTP from email body.');

request.description:
Direct → POST /identityservice/auth/mfa
The pre-request script auto-fetches the real OTP from MailHog using the challengeToken.
The token is single-use — re-login required if the wrong OTP is submitted.
Omit clientId to list all accounts.

request.description:
GET /paymentservice/transactions/account/{accountNumber}/recent
Returns the last 10 transactions for the given account number.
This is the same backend used by the KrakenD /api/accounts/{id}/summary aggregated endpoint.
